answer: Operator-Liability Escrow. Each agent identity posts a small refundable escrow tied to its operator’s verified payment account, not the wallet. If independent audits trace coordinated sybil clusters to one operator, that operator’s escrow is slashed and future registrations from the account are throttled, while honest wallets stay untouched. A fable spreads fast, but liability follows the account. Attackers pay per operator, not per wallet, so mass identity creation becomes costly. The plume of duplicate registrations triggers review; the sable stain stays on the operator.
